extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in geometric analysis / differential geometry studying Ricci flow with surgery and 3-manifold geometrization
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria, estimates, and structural decompositions used to analyze long-time behavior of Ricci flow with δ-cutoff surgery on compact 3-manifolds (curvature/volume assumptions, canonical neighborhoods, thick-thin decomposition, and consequences leading to geometrization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume monotonicity under surgery (V(t)(t+3/2)^{-3/2} nonincreasing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since the cutoff surgeries do not increase volume, inequality (7.6.3)/(7.6.4) shows d/dt log V(t) / (t + 3/2) ... ≤ 0; equivalently the function V(t) (t + 3/2)^{-3/2} is nonincreasing on [0, +∞).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to compare volumes at different times and to control total volume in long-time arguments; explicitly appears in (7.6.3) and (7.6.4) and is invoked when extracting geometric limits and in counting persistent hyperbolic pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.1 — limits of parabolic rescalings have constant sectional curvature
rubrics_metrics.description: If for a fixed 0 < r < 1 and a sequence of times t_α → ∞ the rescalings of the solution on parabolic neighborhoods P(x_α,t_α,r√t_α, r^2 t_α) with factor (t_α)^{-1} (and time shift) converge in C^∞ to some smooth limiting solution, then the limiting solution has constant sectional curvature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a criterion used to deduce that any smooth limit of appropriately rescaled regions is a space form; it is the key-to-conclude-from-local-estimates-to-global-hyperbolic-limits step used repeatedly (see application in Lemma 7.6.2 and Theorem 7.6.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Curvature control from local volume lower bound (estimate (7.6.7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a geodesic ball Bt0(x0,r0√t0) with volume ≥ c_w (r0√t0)^3 and lower sectional curvature bound, there exist constants τ,K,K' (depending only on w, ε) so that on the parabolic neighborhood P(x0,t0,r0√t0/4, −τ (r0√t0)^2) one has R < K(r0√t0)^{-2} and |Rm| ≤ K' (r0√t0)^{-2}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative curvature bound is used to obtain smooth subsequential limits after rescaling; constants depend only on the volume parameter w and the surgery/accuracy parameter ε (see Theorem 7.5.2 inputs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2(i) — local volume + lower curvature bound → smallness of |2t R_ij + g_ij| at center
rubrics_metrics.description: For any ε>0 and given w>0, r>0, ξ>0 there is T = T(w,r,ξ,ε) such that if at time t0 ≥ T the geodesic ball Bt0(x0, r√t0) has volume at least w (r√t0)^3 and sectional curvature ≥ −(r√t0)^{-2}, then at (x0,t0) we have |2tR_ij + g_ij| < ξ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides quantitative closeness (after scaling) to a hyperbolic metric at the center of a sufficiently large-time, non-collapsed ball with controlled lower curvature; T depends on w,r,ξ,ε. It is the basic 'local almost-hyperbolic' test used when identifying thick regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2(ii) — extension of (i) to larger spatial balls
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the assumptions of (i) and given A<+∞, one can ensure the estimate |2tR_ij + g_ij| < ξ holds for all points in Bt0(x0, A r√t0) provided T = T(w,r,ξ,A,ε) is chosen large enough.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows control on larger spatial scales (factor A) by increasing the required waiting time T; used to show whole thick regions are almost hyperbolic, not just single points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 7.6.2(iii) — parabolic (space-time) extension
rubrics_metrics.description: The same smallness estimate |2tR_ij + g_ij| < ξ holds throughout the forward parabolic neighborhood P(x0,t0,A r√t0, A r^2 t0) for sufficiently large T depending on parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives control in time as well as space: once a region is almost hyperbolic at time t0, it remains so for a uniform forward time interval, provided t0 is large enough.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption for high-curvature points
rubrics_metrics.description: Points whose scalar curvature is above certain thresholds (e.g. ≥ K1 (r√t0)^{-2}) have canonical neighborhoods (ε-necks or ε-caps) as guaranteed by Theorem 7.5.1 and used in arguments (existence of ε-necks/ε-caps around points with high scalar curvature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to get local geometric models in high-curvature regions and to deduce volume and curvature comparisons; canonical neighborhoods also guide where surgeries may occur and are essential for constructing contradictions in collapsing arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume noncollapsing lower bound on controlled balls (7.6.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given curvature estimates on Bt0(x0, 2A r√t0) one obtains a universal κ = κ(w,r,A,ε) so that Vol_t0(Bt0(x, (K'1)^{-1/2} r√t0)) ≥ κ ((K'1)^{-1/2} r√t0)^3 for any x in Bt0(x0, A r√t0) when t0 large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Bishop–Gromov-type noncollapsing volume lower bound (with constants depending on parameters) is required to apply Lemma 7.6.1 and extract smooth limits; it ties curvature control to volume control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thick-thin decomposition (Theorem 7.6.3) — thin part criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For given w>0 and small ε>0 there exists ρ=ρ(w,ε)>0 such that for large t the manifold decomposes Mt = M_thin(w,t) ∪ M_thick(w,t). For x∈M_thin there exists r=r(x,t)>0 with 0<r√t<ρ√t such that Rm ≥ −(r√t)^{-2} on Bt(x,r√t) and Vol_t(Bt(x,r√t)) < w (r√t)^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thin points are those which are (locally) nonnegatively pinched below by a scale r and yet have very small volume compared to the Euclidean/hyperbolic model — i.e., locally collapsed regions with controlled lower curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thick-thin decomposition (Theorem 7.6.3) — thick part criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: For x∈M_thick(w,t) we have |2t R_ij + g_ij| < ξ on Bt(x,ρ√t) and Vol_t(Bt(x,ρ√t)) ≥ (1/10) w (ρ√t)^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thick points are quantitatively close (after scaling by t^{-1}) to constant negative-curvature metrics on balls of fixed radius ρ√t and are noncollapsed; these are the regions that may converge to hyperbolic pieces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling limits of thick points → finite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: If x_α ∈ M_thick(w,t_α) with t_α → ∞, then scalings of g_ij(t_α) around x_α by factor (t_α)^{-1} converge smoothly (along a subsequence) to a complete hyperbolic manifold of finite volume with constant sectional curvature −1/4 (up to normalization scaling used in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the key identification: thick-region blow-ups produce hyperbolic geometric limits, motivating the extraction of persistent hyperbolic pieces in the long-time picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-time behavior trichotomy (Theorem 7.6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For normalized initial data and appropriate surgery parameters, one of three alternatives holds: (i) for all sufficiently large t, Mt = M_thin(w,t); (ii) there exists a sequence t_α such that the rescaled essential component (t_α)^{-1} g_ij(t_α) converges in C^∞ to a hyperbolic metric on the initial compact manifold M; or (iii) there is a finite collection of complete noncompact finite-volume hyperbolic 3‑manifolds H_l and compact truncations K_l which (after diffeomorphisms into Mt for large t) approximate the metric (t^{-1} g_ij(t)) arbitrarily closely on each K_l, and the complements of these embedded K_l sit inside the thin part M_thin(w,t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the global dichotomy/trichotomy describing whether the manifold collapses, becomes globally hyperbolic, or decomposes into persistent hyperbolic pieces plus thin regions; it is the central structural theorem driving geometrization via Ricci flow with surgery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incompressibility of boundary tori of persistent hyperbolic pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: For persistent hyperbolic pieces embedded into Mt and truncated along small-area constant-mean-curvature tori, the boundary tori are incompressible in Mt (i.e., the inclusion induces injection on π1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Meeks–Yau/Meeks–Simon–Yau existence of area-minimizing disks spanning kernel curves and an area-evolution inequality (7.6.21) showing such minimal disk area would decrease at a nonintegrable rate, contradiction; this incompressibility is necessary to realize the torus decomposition in the geometrization picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgeries do not increase volume (procedural constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: By construction the δ-cutoff surgeries remove high-curvature caps and do not increase the total volume of the manifold; this is repeatedly invoked (e.g., in deriving monotonicity of V(t)(t+3/2)^{-3/2} and in persistence arguments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A structural property of the surgery procedure that allows comparison of pre- and post-surgery volumes and is essential for volume-based collapse/noncollapse arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's Claim / Shioya–Yamaguchi weaker assertion (collapse ⇒ graph manifold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman's Claim: For a sequence of compact orientable 3‑manifolds (possibly with convex boundary) with local balls B(x,ρ) of volume ≤ w_α ρ^3 and sectional curvature ≥ −ρ^{-2} (and controlled small-diameter/curvature collars on boundary), for sufficiently large α the manifolds are diffeomorphic to graph manifolds. Shioya–Yamaguchi proved a weaker assertion for closed manifolds (no boundary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This collapsing criterion (local volume collapse with lower curvature bound implies graph-manifold topology) is used as the final ingredient to classify the thin parts and conclude geometrization; authors note reliance on the weaker proved assertion when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prime decomposition and definition of geometrization (background topological standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prime Decomposition Theorem: every compact orientable 3‑manifold decomposes as a finite connected sum of orientable prime 3‑manifolds. Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture: a compact orientable prime 3‑manifold admits a finite collection of disjoint incompressible tori so that each component of the complement admits a locally homogeneous Riemannian metric of finite volume (one of Thurston's eight geometries).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These topology-theoretic standards are the target classification statements for Ricci flow: the analytic long-time and collapsing results are assembled to satisfy the topological decomposition and geometric model conclusions of geometrization.
